_readme: Prices read off Pokemon Center's own TCG cards category page, product by
product, with the path to each product so a reader can check the figure.
WHAT IT IS. 431 products and their prices, read from
https://www.pokemoncenter.com/category/tcg-cards on August 17, 2026, in two
passes on that day.
THE FIRST PASS CLAIMED THE WHOLE CATEGORY AND HAD A TENTH OF IT. It recorded
31 products, and this file said of them: 'That was the whole category page: no
pagination control was present, so this is all of it rather than the first
screen of it.' The second pass walked the category to its end and found TEN
PAGES, a counter reading 591 of 591, and 400 distinct product paths. NOT ONE
of those 400 is among the first pass's 31. Two passes, one day, one url, and
the sets do not overlap at all, so the listing this page hands you is a window
onto the catalogue rather than the catalogue. Never conclude you have all of
something here because no Next button was on the screen, and never let a count
in this file be quoted as the size of Pokemon's range.
WHY IT IS ITS OWN FILE. data/msrp.json joins to it on the exact `name`, the
same way that file joins to data/pack-counts-current.json on `productName`.
So a price printed on /msrp.html traces to a row here, which carries the
product path it was read off and the date it was read, and scripts/build-msrp.mjs
FAILS THE BUILD if the two ever disagree. One reading, one place.
KEEP THE PATHS. They are the only way a reader can go and check a price for
themselves, and the only way a later re-read can match a row to the one it
replaces. A name can be re-worded by the shop; a product path is the SKU.
`name` IS THE SHOP'S OWN PRODUCT TITLE WITH TWO MECHANICAL EDITS AND NO
OTHERS. The boilerplate prefix 'Pokemon TCG: ' or 'Pokemon Trading Card Game: '
is dropped, because it is on almost every title and carries nothing, and the
accented characters are folded to ASCII (e to e, curly to straight quote, em
dash to hyphen) to match the rest of this repo. Everything else is left alone,
INCLUDING THE ERA PREFIX. 'Scarlet & Violet-', 'Sword & Shield-' and
'Mega Evolution-' are the single most useful field in this file after the
price: they are how you tell current stock from a decade of back catalogue,
and every generational price rise recorded on /msrp.html was found with them.
THE 31 FROM THE FIRST PASS WERE SHORTENED FURTHER, BY HAND, and were left that
way rather than rewritten. So this file holds two naming conventions and you
can tell them apart by whether the era prefix is present. That is untidy and it
is deliberate: renaming them would rewrite the `pcFrom` join keys in
data/msrp.json for no gain, and the path is the identity in both conventions.
TWO PRODUCTS CAN SHARE A NAME AND THEY DO. 'V Heroes Tin (Espeon V)' is TWO
SKUs, 699-17151 at $19.99 and 699-17163 at $24.99, both live on August 17, 2026.
'Collector Chest (Fall 2023)' is two SKUs at the same price. resolvePC() in
scripts/build-msrp.mjs therefore resolves a `pcFrom` name to EVERY row that
carries it and fails the build if they disagree on price, rather than taking
whichever one a Map happened to keep. Do not delete a duplicate to make a join
work: the duplicate is the finding.
POKEMONCENTER.COM DOES NOT ANSWER A SCRIPT. A plain HTTP fetch of any url on
it returns a short bot-check page with no product data on it. THIS FILE WAS
READ BY A PERSON DRIVING A REAL BROWSER, which is the only way the page loads,
and re-reading it means doing that again by hand, all ten pages of it.
DO NOT AUTOMATE IT AND DO NOT WORK AROUND THE CHECK. Do not fetch the site
from a builder, do not add it to any sync script, and do not hotlink its
images. A route that looks like it works is suspicious rather than lucky.
`img` IS A URL THIS REPO HAS RECORDED, NOT ONE IT USES. Sixteen rows carry
one. They are Pokemon Center's own product photographs and the shape is
/images/DAMRoot/Thumbnail/<bucket>/P<internalId>_<SKU>_01.jpg
where <SKU> is the segment already in `path` and the other two parts are NOT
derivable from anything else in this file. That is why there are sixteen and
not 431: they have to be read off the page at the same time as the price, and
the second pass captured prices without them. A later pass that wants the rest
must collect the img src alongside the name in the same sweep.
NOTHING ON THIS SITE LOADS THESE URLS AND NOTHING SHOULD START TO without a
decision being made first. /msrp.html illustrates its rows with TCGplayer
thumbnails through the PHOTOS map in scripts/build-msrp.mjs. Hotlinking
Pokemon's shop is forbidden above; using the images at all is a separate
question about a fan site and official artwork, and it has not been answered
here. Recording the address is not the same as deciding to fetch it.
A POKEMON CENTER PRICE IS AN MSRP. Pokemon Center is The Pokemon Company's own
shop selling its own product, so what it charges IS what the manufacturer
suggests, and that is the whole of what MSRP means. THIS FILE USED TO SAY THE
OPPOSITE. It said 'it is still not a published MSRP. The Pokemon Company
publishes no MSRP list, which /msrp.html says and must keep saying.' That was
wrong and the page no longer says it. The true and much narrower finding is
that NO DOCUMENT TITLED MSRP EXISTS: pokemon.com's product showcases itemise
contents and state no price, and press.pokemon.com carries none either. A
missing price LIST is not a missing price. Do not reintroduce the old wording.
A PRICE HERE IS STILL A PRICE ON A DATE. A shop price moves, including the
manufacturer's own, which is why every figure carries the day it was read.
A reading is also ONE PRODUCT. Two Tech Sticker Collections at $14.99 is
evidence about Tech Sticker Collections; one Ultra-Premium Collection at
$119.99 is a fact about that box and not about the type, because the type
genuinely runs to $179.99 elsewhere.
AND ONE PRODUCT TYPE HAS TWO PRICES HERE MORE OFTEN THAN NOT, because this
shop sells a decade of back catalogue beside this month's box. The split is
usually GENERATIONAL and the era prefix is what shows it: Build & Battle Boxes
are $19.99 for every Sword & Shield set and $21.99 for every Scarlet & Violet
and Mega Evolution one, and there is no overlap. Where the split is clean like
that, /msrp.html prices the current line and names the older figure. Where two
prices are live WITHIN the current line, as with Tech Sticker Collections at
$14.99 and $15.99, that page prints no number at all. Averaging them, or
picking the one that appears more often, is the failure this file exists to
prevent.
NOTHING IS EDITED ON THE WAY IN. Prices are as read. If a figure looks wrong,
re-read the page in a browser and replace the row with the new reading and the
new date. Do not correct it here from memory or from another site.
